headline: Beats EPS guidance; trims outlook on EMEA weakness
summary_short: PVH Corp. posted first-quarter revenue of $2.03 billion (+2.1% y/y), ahead of guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.01 topping the $1.65-$1.80 guided range; GAAP net income of $88 million reversed a $44.8 million prior-year loss.
summary_long: Revenue rose 2.1% to $2.025 billion, ahead of guidance, as APAC (+10%) and direct-to-consumer growth (+6%) offset EMEA and Americas softness from Middle East-related demand pressure and wholesale timing shifts. Gross margin held flat at 58.6%. Non-GAAP EBIT fell 18% y/y on planned brand investment; GAAP net income swung to $88 million from a $44.8 million loss, mainly reflecting the absence of last year's $480 million goodwill impairment. PVH lowered full-year revenue guidance to approximately flat (from a prior slight increase) on prolonged EMEA weakness, while reaffirming full-year non-GAAP operating margin (~8.8%) and EPS ($11.80-$12.10) guidance. Cash rose to $592.5 million; inventory fell 5% y/y; no Q1 buybacks.

drivers.explanation: Delivered on Q1 plan, beat EPS guidance, and grew direct-to-consumer in stores and e-commerce across both Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger per CEO commentary.
APAC (+10%, partly Lunar New Year timing) and direct-to-consumer (+6%) growth offset EMEA and Americas declines tied to Middle East-driven demand pressure and a wholesale shipment timing shift.
Margin held at 58.6% y/y as tariff and promotional pressure plus licensed-category mix drag were offset by mitigation actions, favorable mix, and lower product costs including FX.
Non-GAAP EBIT declined as planned marketing and brand-investment spending increased, partly offset by a $12M positive FX impact.
Swing to profit from a prior-year loss is explained almost entirely by the absence of the $480M goodwill and intangible impairment charge taken in Q1 2025.
Company cites continued focus on inventory productivity and a data- and demand-driven operating model as the general driver, without quarter-specific detail.
